## Historical audit — S0004

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_2/results/r2/fixed_h/H0/fixed_version_test/commons_92056365/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. Observations are complete lines, so no split-observation offsets are needed.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — line 1, student `model_request` | Reconstruct an indoor photograph as separate 3D meshes, matching viewpoint, framing, placement, colors and materials. The reference image is identified but not visible in this audit; “daylit diner” is the student’s interpretation, not independently verified scene content. |
| Construction — lines 3–4, student `model_response` and `execute` step 1 | The nonempty program specifies many objects: tiled floor, ceiling, window structures, booths, tables, chairs, lamps and plants. It groups furniture parts into assets and rotates chairs; this establishes intended part relationships and poses, not verified physical connections or correct placement. |
| Appearance and view — lines 3–4 | The code assigns colors and a uniform mesh-material roughness, with no explicit image textures. It specifies a camera, world illumination, three area lights and Cycles render settings. Whether materials, perspective, lighting, occlusion or framing match the reference is unknown. |
| Exploration and teacher — lines 1–4 | One autonomous program and execution are visible. The student session reports zero tool calls; there is no visible teacher input, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption, and no visible iteration following feedback. |
| Validation and outcome — line 5, `execution_result` | Blender timed out after about 454.6 seconds; `ok` is false, stdout and stderr are empty, and `image` is null. This is a **technical interruption**, not evidence of a geometric or algorithmic failure. No successful build, rendered comparison, formal success, partial-correctness finding or final submission is visible. |

**Lessons and uncertainty.** A transferable caution is that a detailed procedural scene is not validated merely by being generated: execution and visual inspection are separate steps. The large number of tiled and plant primitives is a task-specific hypothesis for the timeout, not a demonstrated cause; the trace gives no progress log. The actual reference content, whether geometry was fully created before timeout, and whether a simpler scene would have completed or matched better remain unresolved.
